source_fields.query_signature: Choose an arm $x_t$, then observe all $m$ reward coordinates of that arm. Conditional on past observations and the current arm, each coordinate is $1$-sub-Gaussian around its fixed mean; coordinates need not be independent. $$\mathbb E\!\left[e^{s(Y_{t,i}-\mu_i(x_t))}\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},x_t\right]\le e^{s^2/2}\qquad(s\in\mathbb R,\ 1\le i\le m).$$ Causal policies may use the public covering and activation interfaces. The metric space, $m,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$, and $\lambda\ge\lambda_\star$ are public. The mean functions and lexicographically optimal arm $x^\star$ are hidden. Observed feedback may be stored and reused computationally; unrevealed past information and additional queries to exhausted samples are unavailable. Any within-round full-function or common-sample two-point access must be explicitly specified.

target_object_registry.definition: The action set is a public metric space $(\mathcal X,D)$ of diameter at most $1$, possibly with infinitely many arms; the required covering and activation interfaces are available. Each arm has $m$ fixed mean rewards $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m$, ordered by priority, and every mean function is $1$-Lipschitz. Each objective has oscillation at most $1$; irrelevant common additive shifts are unrestricted. A lexicographically optimal arm $x^\star$ exists. Ties are allowed at each priority; subsequent objectives are compared among arms optimal for all higher-priority objectives. The tradeoff coefficient is finite: $$\lambda_\star=\inf\!\left\{\lambda\ge0:\ \mu_i(x)-\mu_i(x^\star)\le\lambda\max_{j<i}\bigl(\mu_j(x^\star)-\mu_j(x)\bigr),\ \forall x\in\mathcal X,\ 2\le i\le m\right\}<\infty.$$ $$N_c(r)=\min\!\left\{n:\ \mathcal X\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{n}B_D(x_j,r),\ x_j\in\mathcal X\right\}.$$ Here $N_c(r)$ is the covering number at radius $r$. The objective-specific zooming quantities $N_z^{(i)}(r)$ use the source definitions on the corresponding near-optimal regions and cannot be replaced by the ambient dimension $d$.

source_fields.query_signature: At round t, choose one arm $X_t\in\mathcal X$ using past observations and independent internal randomness, then receive both coordinates $(Y_t^1,Y_t^2)$. Conditional on the past and current arm, $\mathbb E[\exp(\theta(Y_t^i-\mu^i(X_t)))\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},X_t]\le\exp(\theta^2/2)$ for all real theta and i=1,2. Cross-coordinate independence is not required. No unselected-arm feedback, same-round second pull, or historical requery is provided. Public inputs are T, the fact m=2, the compact metric and its anchor-plus-tie geometry, and the finite supplied upper bound lambda. No external confidence parameter is required by this expected-regret view. Mean functions, the primary-optimal arm set, and the lexicographic optimum are hidden. A measurable maximal-net oracle is available: given a nonempty compact subset U of the public metric space and a radius r>0, it returns a finite inclusion-maximal r-separated subset of U. Such a set covers U by closed radius-r balls. This geometric computation does not supply reward information and is not charged as an arm pull.

definition.arms: known metric (X,D) of diameter <=1, each mu_i is 1-Lipschitz; required covering/activation oracles are available
definition.objectives: m ordered objectives with a lexicographically optimal arm x_star (ties allowed)
definition.tradeoff: lambda_star=inf{lambda>=0: mu_i(x)-mu_i(x_star)<=lambda max_{j<i}[mu_j(x_star)-mu_j(x)] for all i>=2,x}; restrict to finite lambda_star
definition.mean_range: objective mean ranges have diameter <=1; additive offsets are immaterial

steps: Select arm $x_t$ first, then observe all $m$ coordinates of its reward vector.
Given the past and the current arm, each reward coordinate is conditionally $1$-sub-Gaussian around its fixed mean. Independence between objective coordinates is not required.
Causal strategies may use the public metric-covering or activation interface. The metric space, $m,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$, and $\lambda\ge\lambda_\star$ are public.
Mean functions and the lexicographically optimal arm $x^\star$ are hidden.
